subject.title: fix: harden Mattermost slash callback auth

question: Should OpenClaw fail closed for Mattermost native slash command registration when the resolved callback URL is not HTTPS, including explicit HTTP callbacks?
rationale: This is a token-bearing callback security boundary, but the safer default can break existing HTTP callback deployments during upgrade, so automation should not decide the policy tradeoff alone.

options.title: Require HTTPS before merge
options.body: Accept the security hardening after redacted real Mattermost proof shows HTTPS registration still works and HTTP registration fails closed before command registration.

options.title: Stage the compatibility break
options.body: Ask for a staged or opt-in strict mode if maintainers want to preserve existing HTTP deployments for one release cycle.

options.title: Reject fail-closed transport policy
options.body: Close or replace the PR if maintainers decide HTTP callback deployments remain supported despite the token transport risk.

recommendation.title: Require HTTPS before merge
recommendation.body: Accept the security hardening after redacted real Mattermost proof shows HTTPS registration still works and HTTP registration fails closed before command registration.

likelyOwner.reason: eleqtrizit owns the most recent merged slash callback validation refresh that overlaps the security boundary being changed here.
